newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan daily's poll shows Japan-U.S. ties on mend.
newsitem.headline: Japan daily's poll shows Japan-U.S. ties on mend.

text.p: Nearly half of Japanese and Americans surveyed in a Japanese newspaper poll believe relations between the two countries are good, the mass-circulation Yomiuri Shimbun said on Monday.
It also said that nearly two out of three people questioned in both countries see China as a potential military threat.

The Yomiuri, in a poll conducted with the Gallup Organisation in January and February, found that 46 percent of people asked in both Japan and the United States consider bilateral ties to be "very good" or "good".

The survey results represent a 23 percentage point improvement in sentiment among Japanese about bilateral relations and an 18 point improvement among U.S. respondents from the previous survey in 1995, when bilateral ties were strained by trade disputes over cars and car parts.
In addition to their shared sense of improved relations, both U.S. and Japanese respondents showed a common perception of China as a potential threat, the newspaper said.

Some 60 percent of U.S. respondents and 64 percent of Japanese said they feared China could become a military threat, according to the survey. More than 73 percent of the Japanese said they felt threatened by China's growing economic power.

Asked which country was most likely to pose a military threat to Japan, North Korea topped the Japanese respondents' list with 55 percent, followed by China with some 39 percent and Russia with just under 35 percent.
U.S. respondents to the multiple choice survey put the Middle East region first with almost 50 percent, followed by China with 41 percent and Russia with 33 percent, the newspaper said.
The survey polled 2,030 Japanese aged 20 or above and 1,032 Americans aged 18 or older, the Yomiuri said.
